candidates.name: Museum Municipal du Patrimoine Amazigh
candidates.content: The museum which exhibits a small collection of Berber objects from 18th and 19th century the likes of old Berber music instruments, Berber jewelry, traditional clothing and old manuscripts.

candidates.name: Memory of Agadir Museum
candidates.content: The sign is missing: you go through iron gates on the corner. Mostly photographic exhibits which concentrate on the Agadir earthquake on 29 February 1960. Cost is 20-30 dirham each and there is a guide who speaks Arabic, French an

candidates.name: Coco Polizzi's Medina
candidates.content: Coco Polizzi has been recreating a traditional Moroccan Medina on route N1 in Bensergao. Out of town you will need to take an orange Petit taxi, and arrange a time for the taxi to return to collect you, but its well worth the effo

candidates.name: Fortress
candidates.content: There's part of the original fortress which is at the top of the hill beside the city, over the huge painting. It's possible to walk up there, taxi will cost 30-50 dirham.

candidates.name: Zoo
candidates.content: This is a small zoo, called "Vallée des Oiseaux" ('Birds Valley'). There is a very nice cage you can walk inside, many birds from all the world, some goat-like animals from the Atlas, and even exotic mammals. The children of Agadi

candidates.name: Souk El Had
candidates.content: With over 3000 stalls the souk is a must see. Everything from tourist souvenirs, clothes, leather goods, household items, to fruit and veg. If you are a tourist and enter via Gate 9 or 10 (the main gates) expect to be approached b

candidates.name: Adrar Stadium
candidates.content: This is multi-use but mostly for soccer, with a capacity of 45,480. The home team is Hassania Agadir, playing in Botola Pro the top tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.

candidates.name: Surfing
candidates.content: Imesouane, Devils rock (at the town of Tamragh and with the neighbouring towns of Aourir and Taghazout), Anchor point, Cro-Cro and many others. There are a lot of surf schools and surf camps and surf shop. The best surf season fro

candidates.name: Golf
candidates.content: With three top-notch golf courses, Agadir can rival most countries' golf facilities. Ask at any large hotel about the bus transport which collects visitors several times a day.

candidates.name: Beach
candidates.content: The main attraction is the beach, which is very big and not very crowded. The beach is very windy, at least in February.

candidates.name: K-moon
candidates.content: Small restaurant with excellent grilled meat over a wood fire and lots of small bowls filled with different things. The welcome is pleasant and the food fresh and tasty. Quick and efficient service.

candidates.name: L'étoile d'Agadir
candidates.content: Friendly and typical restaurant, traditional cuisine. A lot of nostalgia in this place. Very good restaurant with local specialties. Very tasty tagine and couscous.

candidates.name: Herguita
candidates.content: Fantastic location with view of the ocean. Typical, good food. Best brochette.

candidates.name: Rotisserie Al Marché شواية المارشي
candidates.content: If you're looking for a Moroccan street food experience, this one is for you. Authentic place. Best sandwiches.

candidates.name: Restaurant les trois chaudrons
candidates.content: Homemade Moroccan taste. Very good welcome and nice service.

candidates.name: Bab Agadir
candidates.content: Typical Moroccan restaurant. Warm welcome, excellent meal couscous tajines. Staff super friendly, great food.
